problem: "Gate current starts regeneration" uses an unexplained word. A student who has not yet met the two-transistor model will not know what regeneration means here.
fix: An SCR latches on when gate current starts the regenerative action inside the four layers: each of the two internal transistors supplies the base current of the other, so the current keeps itself on.

problem: tc = C × V / I silently assumes the load current stays constant at I while the capacitor charges or discharges. Without that assumption the formula does not follow, and students will apply it to circuits where the current changes.
fix: State the assumption: tc = C × V / I holds when the load current is constant at I during commutation; if the current changes with time, tc is the time for the capacitor to swing by V at that current and must be found from the actual waveform.

problem: "Wide band-gap devices have short tq" is loose. tq is a thyristor datasheet quantity; MOSFETs and IGBTs are not thyristors and are turned off from the gate, so they do not have a tq in this sense.
fix: SiC and GaN switches turn off very fast, so in those converters the reverse-bias window is limited by circuit inductance and gate drive rather than by a device tq.
